- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase early horizon lows and add buffer for sudden crashes.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 4.39, 12.59, 16.59) — cap forecast peaks at 2x recent high or 1.5x 18-day moving average to prevent overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 1.00, 0.33), model tends to misalign horizon — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for 30d forecasts.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) for 5+ days, model often underperforms — increase baseline forecast by 5–15% to account for suppressed volatility.
